rules.title: Manifest is line-oriented key/value
rules.statement: A module manifest is parsed line by line. Each non-empty, non-comment line is split into a key (first whitespace-delimited token) and a value (remainder, trimmed). Surrounding whitespace on the line is trimmed before parsing.

rules.title: Blank and # comment lines ignored
rules.statement: A manifest line that is empty after trimming, or whose first non-whitespace character is '#', is ignored.

rules.title: Unknown directives ignored for forward compatibility
rules.statement: A manifest key that matches no known directive is silently ignored (forward compatibility); it is not an error.

rules.title: Recognized manifest directives
rules.statement: Recognized manifest directives are: `module` (canonical name), `version`, `id` (mangle key), `root` (source directory), `depends`, `exclude`, `ast_only`, `lowering`, `tier`, `prelude`. `depends`/`exclude`/`ast_only` accumulate one value per occurrence (empty values skipped); the rest set a single value.

rules.title: module and root are required
rules.statement: A manifest is invalid (parse fails with an error) unless it declares a non-empty `module` name and a non-empty `root` directory.

rules.title: Version defaults to 0.0
rules.statement: If no `version` directive is present, the module version defaults to "0.0".

rules.title: lowering directive: lazy|eager, default eager
rules.statement: The `lowering` directive must be exactly `lazy` or `eager`; any other value is an error. Absent the directive, lowering is eager (emit .o + LIR blob); `lazy` emits only the parsed-AST artifact and defers lowering to the consumer.

rules.title: tier directive restricted to lang|mem|std
rules.statement: The `tier` directive must be exactly one of `lang`, `mem`, or `std`; any other (including empty) value is an error. lang = no-alloc/no-OS, mem = heap/no-OS, std = full. An absent tier means tier-not-declared (no availability enforcement).

rules.title: prelude requires a package name
rules.statement: If a `prelude` directive is present, its value must be a non-empty (dotted) package name; an empty value is an error. The named package is injected as an implicit `use <pkg>;` at the head of every file in the module that lacks `#![no_implicit_prelude]`.

rules.title: Effective module id: explicit id else path hash
rules.statement: The effective module identifier used in symbol mangling is the explicit manifest `id` (sanitized) when set; otherwise it is derived as the FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the module's target install path, formatted as 'm' followed by 16 lowercase hex digits. The 'm' prefix guarantees the token never begins with a digit.

rules.title: Module id sanitized to mangle-legal token
rules.statement: An explicit module `id` is sanitized into a mangle-legal token: every character that is not [A-Za-z0-9_] is replaced by '_'. The resulting token is what is baked into symbol mangling to disambiguate same-named packages from different modules/versions.
